summary: In Notion you create a public connection, set a redirect address and choose which workspaces can install it. A Marketplace listing is optional and Notion says to expect to hear back in 5 to 10 business days. One line on Notion's authorization page hints at a review step before you get your authorization URL, and the pages read do not settle it.

verdict.headline: A few hours of setup. Marketplace listing is optional, and Notion says to expect a reply in 5 to 10 business days. Whether Notion must approve a public connection before others can use it is not stated, so test it.

wait.label: Unclear for OAuth itself. Reply within 5 to 10 business days for the optional listing

prerequisites.detail: You pick it when you create the connection.
Any workspace or selected workspaces. You cannot change it later.

prerequisites.item: A server to hold the client secret and tokens
prerequisites.detail: Keep them out of source control.

steps.title: Choose the installation scope
steps.detail: Pick Any workspace if you may ever list on the Marketplace. The scope is fixed at creation, so changing your mind means creating a new connection.

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: You provide a name, development workspace, redirect URI or URIs, installation scope and capabilities.

steps.title: Copy your credentials and authorization URL
steps.detail: The client ID and secret are on the Configuration tab. Notion's page says the authorization URL appears after the connection is submitted for review.

steps.title: Send users to authorize
steps.detail: Include your client ID, redirect URI, response_type=code and owner=user. State is optional but useful against forged requests.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens on your server
steps.detail: Use HTTP Basic auth with your client ID and secret. The response includes access and refresh tokens, a bot ID and workspace details.

steps.title: Save the new token pair on every refresh
steps.detail: Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so the old pair is no longer the one to keep.

steps.title: Optionally list on the Marketplace
steps.detail: Create a listing in the Marketplace dashboard and submit it. Notion's team reviews every submission and says to expect an email reply within 5 to 10 business days.

limits.title: Installation scope is permanent
limits.detail: Selected-workspace connections cannot be listed on the Marketplace.

limits.title: Authorization is per user
limits.detail: Each user authorizes separately and gets their own token for their workspace.

blockers.problem: You chose the wrong installation scope
blockers.why: It cannot be changed after creation.
blockers.nextMove: Create a new connection with the right scope and move your credentials over.

blockers.problem: The authorization URL is not available yet
blockers.why: Notion's page says it appears after the connection is submitted for review, and does not say whether approval is required.
blockers.nextMove: Check the connection settings. If it is waiting on review, ask Notion support and plan for the wait.

blockers.why: Every refresh issues a new refresh token, so reusing an old one fails if you did not save the new pair.
blockers.nextMove: Store both tokens together and update them atomically.

blockers.why: Reasons include brand or trademark issues, quality concerns or missing baseline criteria.
blockers.nextMove: Fix what the email names and resubmit.

agentCanDo: Draft the connection settings and redirect URIs for you to enter
Write the authorize redirect, token exchange and refresh code
Create the Composio auth config once you have a client ID and secret
youMustDo: Create the public connection in your Notion workspace and choose the installation scope
Copy the client secret into your secret store
Submit the Marketplace listing and answer reviewer emails

uncertainties: The pages read do not say whether Notion must approve a public connection before other users can authorize it. The authorization page says the authorization URL appears after submission for review.
How long an access token lasts is not stated on the pages read.

The 5 to 10 business day figure is when Notion says to expect to hear back about the optional Marketplace listing. It is not stated whether that is the decision, and it is not a time for OAuth access.
Not tested hands-on. Creating a connection would settle the approval question in minutes.
